comparisons.peer_summary: Broadcom develops complex digital/mixed signal CMOS and analog III-V semiconductor devices, offering thousands of products for markets including AI networking, data centers, telecommunications, and factory automation.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Broadcom disclose their identity as semiconductor leaders focusing on data centers and AI. AMD defines itself as a 'high performance and adaptive computing leader' powering 'data centers' and 'artificial intelligence (AI)' through its technology portfolio. Broadcom similarly describes itself as developing 'semiconductor devices' for markets including 'artificial intelligence ("AI") networking and connectivity' and 'data center servers'. While both target the same high-growth AI and data center segments, AMD emphasizes its 'adaptive computing' and broad product leadership (CPUs, APUs, SoCs), whereas Broadcom highlights its 'complex digital and mixed signal' and 'analog III-V' device expertise with thousands of products for specific enterprise and connectivity applications.

sentences.text: AMD is the high performance and adaptive computing leader, powering the products and services that help solve the world's most important challenges.

Our technologies advance the future of data centers, powering the cloud services that have become an essential part of how we work, game, and connect to network, PCs, edge computing, and artificial intelligence (AI).
We develop semiconductor devices with a focus on complex digital and mixed signal complementary metal oxide semiconductor ("CMOS") based devices and analog III-V based products.

We offer thousands of products that are used in end products such as enterprise and data center networking, including artificial intelligence ("AI") networking and connectivity, home connectivity, set-top boxes ("STB"), broadband access, telecommunication equipment, smartphones and base stations, data center servers and storage systems, factory automation, power generation and alternative energy systems, and electronic displays.

comparisons.peer_topic: x86 Ecosystem Strategy and Advisory Group
comparisons.peer_summary: Intel's core strategy relies on the x86 ecosystem, advancing it through microarchitectures focused on performance and efficiency. In 2024, the company created an advisory group to expand ecosystem compatibility, simplify software development, and identify future architectural needs.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Intel explicitly frame their business strategies around 'data center' and 'AI' as core market drivers, though they differ in their architectural focus. AMD states its technologies power 'data centers' and 'artificial intelligence (AI)' across 'PCs, edge computing'. Intel similarly states its product offerings serve 'data center to network, PCs, edge computing, and the emerging fields of AI'. A key difference is Intel's emphasis on its foundational 'x86 ecosystem' and recent creation of an advisory group to maintain it, while AMD presents a broader 'high-performance and adaptive computing' leadership claim without restricting its core identity to a single instruction set architecture in this overview section.

sentences.text: Our technologies advance the future of data centers, powering the cloud services that have become an essential part of how we work, game, and connect to network, PCs, edge computing, and artificial intelligence (AI).
We drive innovation through high-performance and adaptive computing technology, software and product leadership.
Lead and democratize compute with Intel x86 and xPU.

Our product offerings provide end-to-end solutions, scaling from data center to network, PCs, edge computing, and the emerging fields of AI and autonomous driving, to serve an increasingly smart and connected world.

comparisons.peer_summary: Due to high capital requirements, Intel is expanding its foundry business for external customers, offering wafer fabrication, packaging, chiplets, and software/services, differentiated by leading-edge technology, committed US/EU capacity, and an IP portfolio including x86 cores.
comparisons.comparison: This comparison concerns the semiconductor manufacturing and product strategy. While AMD discloses its role as a fabless designer delivering 'differentiated solutions' like 'APUs' and 'servers' (implying reliance on foundry partners), Intel discloses its 'foundry business' strategy to serve 'external customers' due to high capital requirements for 'leading-edge semiconductor process technology'. The similarity is that both are central to the semiconductor supply chain's ability to produce advanced computing hardware for AI and data centers. The difference is that AMD is the buyer/designer in this context, while Intel is explicitly expanding its role as a manufacturer (IDM 2.0) for both internal and external use.

sentences.text: With our high-performance product portfolios, we deliver differentiated solutions, such as our semi-custom System-on-Chip (SoCs), Adaptive SoCs, and accelerated processing units (APUs), and platform level client computing devices, embedded platforms and servers for our customers.

The very high capital requirements of modern leading-edge semiconductor process technology development and manufacturing, especially those nodes requiring EUV lithography such as Intel 4, Intel 3, Intel 18A and future nodes, require us to expand the use of our process technologies as they mature and grow the number of wafers produced beyond the expected growth for our own products.

To this end, we are seeking to build a world-class foundry business also serving external customers and have made significant investments in ecosystem support to enable the usage of our manufacturing network by external customers.

comparisons.peer_summary: Micron is an industry leader in innovative memory and storage solutions, delivering high-performance DRAM, NAND, and NOR products through Micron® and Crucial® brands to enable advances in AI and compute-intensive applications.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Micron identify their technologies as critical enablers for the AI and compute-intensive data economy. AMD states it powers 'data centers' and 'artificial intelligence (AI)' through its high-performance products. Micron similarly states its 'innovative memory and storage solutions' fuel 'the data economy, enabling advances in artificial intelligence (AI) and compute-intensive applications'. Both companies position their core business directly within the infrastructure layer required for modern AI workloads, albeit from different vantage points: AMD as compute processors and Micron as memory/storage.

sentences.text: Our technologies advance the future of data centers, powering the cloud services that have become an essential part of how we work, game, and connect to network, PCs, edge computing, and artificial intelligence (AI).
We drive innovation through high-performance and adaptive computing technology, software and product leadership.

Every day, the innovations that our people create fuel the data economy, enabling advances in artificial intelligence (AI) and compute-intensive applications that unleash opportunities - from the data center to the intelligent edge and across the client and mobile user experience.

comparisons.peer_topic: Data Center AI and High-Performance Storage Offerings
comparisons.peer_summary: Demand for AI and big data is driving the need for high-performance storage; SBU addresses this with the 6500 30TB SSD for AI data lakes and sampled the 9550 series in 2024 for AI and high-performance computing workloads.
comparisons.comparison: This comparison links AMD's data center/AI focus with Micron's specific storage solutions for those same workloads. AMD's business overview highlights 'data centers' and 'artificial intelligence' as essential markets powered by its technology. Micron specifically addresses the 'growing use of cloud computing and big data' in data centers, noting that 'Applications such as machine learning servers require fast access to data' and highlighting its SSDs for 'AI data lake applications'. Both disclosures reflect the symbiotic demand for compute (AMD) and storage (Micron) driven by AI and big data analytics trends.

AMD lists 'data centers' and 'artificial intelligence (AI)' as key areas powered by its technology. NVIDIA's segment explicitly includes 'Data Center accelerated computing platforms' and 'AI Enterprise... software'. Both companies are primary suppliers to the same high-performance computing infrastructure market, though NVIDIA emphasizes 'networking' and 'accelerated computing' as part of its specific segment definition, while AMD uses broader 'adaptive computing' terminology.

sentences.text: Our technologies advance the future of data centers, powering the cloud services that have become an essential part of how we work, game, and connect to network, PCs, edge computing, and artificial intelligence (AI).
We drive innovation through high-performance and adaptive computing technology, software and product leadership.

The Compute & Networking segment is comprised of our Data Center accelerated computing platforms and end-to-end networking platforms including Quantum for InfiniBand and Spectrum for Ethernet; our NVIDIA DRIVE automated-driving platform and automotive development agreements; Jetson robotics and other embedded platforms; NVIDIA AI Enterprise and other software; and DGX Cloud software and services.

comparisons.peer_summary: Qualcomm is a global technology leader developing foundational technologies including 3G, 4G, 5G, and on-device AI to power smartphones and connected devices, while scaling innovations into automotive and IoT sectors.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Qualcomm identify themselves as global technology leaders driving innovation in computing and AI, but with different primary end-markets. AMD focuses on 'data centers', 'PCs', and 'edge computing' for AI. Qualcomm focuses on 'smartphones and connected devices' and 'on-device artificial intelligence (AI)', while also scaling into 'automotive and IoT'. The similarity is the shared emphasis on 'AI' and 'high-performance computing' as strategic pillars. The difference lies in AMD's strength in stationary/edge infrastructure (servers/data centers) versus Qualcomm's dominance in mobile and embedded connectivity.

sentences.text: Our technologies advance the future of data centers, powering the cloud services that have become an essential part of how we work, game, and connect to network, PCs, edge computing, and artificial intelligence (AI).
We drive innovation through high-performance and adaptive computing technology, software and product leadership.

We are a global technology leader, helping to bring intelligent computing everywhere through the development and commercialization of foundational technologies, including 3G (third generation), 4G (fourth generation) and 5G (fifth generation) wireless connectivity, high-performance and low-power computing and on-device artificial intelligence (AI).

comparisons.peer_topic: Processor architecture and AI Engine capabilities
comparisons.peer_summary: Qualcomm utilizes System-on-Chip architecture with heterogeneous computing, including Oryon and Kryo CPUs and Adreno GPUs, to enable high-performance, low-power computing. The Qualcomm AI Engine features dedicated hardware and the Hexagon NPU for high-performance on-device AI inference, supported by the AI Stack and AI Hub to simplify developer integration.
comparisons.comparison: This comparison addresses the underlying hardware architecture for AI and computing. AMD describes delivering 'differentiated solutions' including 'accelerated processing units (APUs)' and 'System-on-Chip (SoCs)'. Qualcomm similarly details its 'System-on-Chip (SoC) architecture with heterogeneous computing features' using CPU, GPU, and NPU engines. Both companies utilize SoC architectures to enable 'high-performance' and 'low-power' computing for their respective markets (AMD for desktops/embedded/servers, Qualcomm for mobile/IoT/automotive), highlighting the convergence of compute and AI in silicon design.

sentences.text: With our high-performance product portfolios, we deliver differentiated solutions, such as our semi-custom System-on-Chip (SoCs), Adaptive SoCs, and accelerated processing units (APUs), and platform level client computing devices, embedded platforms and servers for our customers.

We have developed System-on-Chip (SoC) architecture with heterogeneous computing features, which uses our central processing unit (CPU) and different types of specialized engines (graphics processing unit (GPU) and neural processing unit (NPU)) to enable high-performance and low-power computing and other optimization techniques.

The Qualcomm® AI Engine, featured in our Snapdragon platforms and many of our other products, includes dedicated hardware capable of running complex AI use cases at high-performance and low-power on device, while also enhancing privacy and security.
